title: Dataset-aware mixed-precision defaults and calibration signal matrix
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Goal: Define per-model mixed-precision defaults (FP8/INT8 recommendations) that are driven by a small, labelled sample of customer-style workloads and an automated calibration signal matrix. Deliver a prescriptive default plus a compact set of guardrails that ensure safe automated rollouts and deterministic fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each model in the catalog has a recommended default precision and one fallback precision with rationale and calibration metrics. 2) Calibration pipeline runs on representative sample slices and produces an accuracy delta, latency/cost delta, and a safety flag. 3) Console exposes chosen default and guardrail triggers for each model + a confidence band. 4) CI gating prevents rollout if accuracy regression > pre-defined threshold for the model. 5) Documentation and runbook for on-call and solutions engineers.
deliverables:
- Sampling harness that pulls N=1k examples from existing eval corpora and customer telemetry slices.
- Calibration job that collects perplexity/accuracy, token-level divergence, and golden-response similarity metrics.
- Signal matrix that maps dataset characteristics (seq length, domain, temperature sensitivity) to precision viability scores.
- UI fields in model catalog: recommended_precision, fallback_precision, confidence_band, and guardrail_triggers.
- CI check that fails if regression > model-specific threshold.
- Playbook: staged rollout steps (shadow -> canary -> 100%) and emergency rollback steps.
work_items: 1) Build sampling harness (ENG) 2) Implement calibration runner (OPS) 3) Define signal matrix schema + mapping rules (ML/Research) 4) Integrate metrics into console + model metadata (Frontend/Backend) 5) Add CI gating + alerting (SRE)
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: More conservative defaults (prefer FP8 over INT8) reduce customer-visible regressions but increase cost. We prefer model-specific thresholds rather than global.
- Sampling: initial runs will use canonical eval sets for each model family with targeted customer slices for high-usage models. This reduces noise but may miss rare-edge cases.
- Calibration metrics: we include both automatic proxies (log-likelihood, token divergence) and a small set of human-labelled golden checks for high-risk models.
- Rollout: default is to enable recommended precision for new models in Dedicated only; Hosted rollout requires explicit QA signoff for P0/P1 models.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): run calibration on top-50 catalog models, produce recommended defaults and signal scores. Phase 2 (2 weeks): integrate defaults into model metadata and expose in Console. Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable automated canary for Dedicated customers with CI gating; manual opt-in for Hosted. Phase 4: broaden to full catalog and add nightly recalibration job.
validation_tests:
- Regression check: for each model, compute BLEU/ROUGE/LLR delta and fail if delta exceeds model threshold.
- Latency/cost check: ensure token throughput change <= 30% for INT8/FP8 compared to baseline unless approved.
- Semantic drift check: embedding cosine similarity for top-K responses >= 0.95 for non-generative tasks.
- Human spot-check: randomized 50-sample manual review for top-10 revenue-impact models.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New catalog metadata fields emitted to tracing/metrics.
- Alert if nightly recalibration flips recommended_precision more than 10% of catalog in a week.
- Pager if canary regression detected on production traffic > 0.5% of requests for a model.
- Dashboard tile: per-model precision history, calibration score, and recent validation runs.
risks:
- False confidence from small sample sizes; mitigated by confidence_band and conservative fallback.
- Edge-case domains (legal/medical) need manual signoff; these will have security_review_required flagged at project level later.
- CI gating adds release friction; will provide bypass with strict audit logging for emergency fixes.
open_questions:
- What is the canonical list of validation metrics (beyond likelihood and embedding similarity) we standardize on?
- What thresholds per model family are acceptable (suggest starting with 0.5% relative accuracy loss for high-importance models)?
- Should we allow automatic precision changes based on live telemetry (auto-tuning) or require manual approval?
